en: The Hymn to Avalokiteśvara composed by Vāsuki, the King of the Nāgas. Om, homage to Avalokiteśvara!
Wearing matted locks, with gentle and wide eyes, his moon-like face always radiant and serene,
his lotus feet worshipped by gods and asuras alike.
I pay homage to the Lord born from the jewel-lotus. ||1||
To him whose divine eyes are as broad as lotus petals, whose pure vision has purified all false views,
who is moist with the nectar of compassion, and who is the sole eye of the world—
I bow to the Lord born from the jewel-lotus. ||2||
Exceedingly radiant with necklaces, moon-ornaments, and half-moons, with shimmering earrings rubbing against his polished cheeks,
and crowded with millions of rays gathered in a garland of light.
I bow to the Lord born from the jewel-lotus. ||3||
On the path of the awakened Dharma, he is the Dharmadhātuka with a thousand arms, or with two, four, or six arms;
equal to the expanse of space, he possesses infinite arms.
I bow to the Lord born from the jewel-lotus. ||4||
Born from the churning of the ocean of skillful means and wisdom, arising as the cause for the protection of the three realms,
the crown of the Lord of Jinas, produced from the relics of the Jina—
I pay homage to the Lord born from the jewel-lotus. ||5||
I pay homage to the noble Avalokita, the compassionate one toward all sentient beings, who stands upon a lotus, holds a lotus in his hand, and wears matted hair. (6)
The hymn to the Noble Avalokiteśvara composed by the illustrious Vāsuki, King of the Nāgas, is complete.
